title: The Big Zoom
tagline: From Finn all the way to the Sun
dadNotes: Earth is about 12,756 km across. The Moon is about 3,475 km, so about four Moons fit across Earth.
Mars is about 6,792 km across: about half as wide as Earth.
Ceres is about 950 km across. Lay about a hundred Mount Everests (8.8 km) end to end and they nearly stretch across it.
Starship is about 124 metres tall, more than a quarter taller than Big Ben (96 metres).
Jupiter is the biggest planet, and lots and lots of Earths could fit inside it.
The Sun is so big that Earth could fit inside it many times over. Let Finn guess what comes next before you slide.

steps.title: Our home
steps.text: This is Earth, our home. Today we start small, with you, and zoom out all the way to the Sun.
steps.dad: Ask Finn: what do you think we will find at the very end?

steps.title: The Big Zoom
steps.intro: Slide to the right to zoom out one step at a time, and watch each new thing appear.

steps.title: Guess!
steps.prompt: How many Moons would fit across Earth?
steps.reveal: Good guess! About four Moons would fit across Earth. Earth is about 12,756 kilometres wide, and the Moon is about 3,475 kilometres wide.

steps.title: A dwarf planet
steps.text: Ceres is a round rock in space, about 950 kilometres across. It is the biggest object in the asteroid belt, between Mars and Jupiter.
steps.wow: Lay about a hundred Mount Everests end to end, and they nearly stretch across it!

steps.title: Taller than Big Ben
steps.text: Starship is about 124 metres tall. That is more than a quarter taller than Big Ben!

steps.title: The giant planet
steps.text: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our Solar System. Lots and lots of Earths could fit inside it.
steps.wow: About 11 Earths would fit across it!

steps.title: The Sun
steps.text: This is the Sun, the star in the middle of our Solar System. Every planet goes round it, and it is the biggest thing we have zoomed to.
steps.wow: About 109 Earths would fit across it!
steps.dad: Ask Finn: what do you think is even bigger than the Sun?

debrief: What do you think is even bigger than the Sun?
